prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout of a workshop from a downward-angled egocentric viewpoint, showing a floor plane receding from the camera wearer's feet and lower torso at the bottom (~0.4–0.8 m away in frames 3–5) toward background tables and a blue chair at 3–5 m, with a central vertical column and leaning wooden boards spanning 0.5–2.0 m in front and to the left. To the right of the boards (~0.3–0.6 m from them and narrowing from ~1.5 m to ~0.8 m from the camera wearer across the five frames), a standing person in a grey sweatshirt faces left toward the boards and away from the camera wearer's gaze, while tools on the floor sit further right at ~1.5–2.2 m. Across frames 1 to 5, increasing brightness shows the camera wearer approaching the boards and extending a left arm in frame 5 to touch a board within arm's reach (~0.5 m), while the other person reaches forward with both arms (~0.4–0.6 m in front of their torso) to hold the upright panels as their head and right side are partly cropped by the right frame edge. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradients clearly separate the layered distances of overlapping pale wooden panels, the vertical column, and the reaching forearms against the similarly coloured wood and sawdust pile below. However, the depth map is unreliable near the upper-left tips of the boards in frames 1–3 where brightness saturates and merges adjacent planks with the column, as well as on the blurred head in frame 2 where a halo inflates the apparent silhouette.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the standing co-worker on the right (pink mask, ~0.8–1.5 m from the camera wearer) and the camera wearer's own lower body and reaching left arm at the bottom of frames 3–4 (brown mask, ~0.3–0.6 m away), while leaving the surrounding workshop floor, column, and wooden boards unmasked in black. Across the five frames, the pink mask shifts closer and enlarges as the camera wearer approaches and turns slightly right, showing the co-worker in left-facing profile reaching left with both hands into the upright boards within their arm's reach (~0.4–0.6 m), with their head, back, and lower legs partially cut off at the top and right borders or occluded by the boards. In frames 3 and 4, the brown mask at the bottom centre and left localizes the camera wearer's legs and outstretched left hand ~0.5–1.0 m below and in front of the co-worker before thecamera wearer's reaching arm in frame 5 goes completely undetected. While the masks help distinguish human limbs from the cluttered background in frames 1–3, the segmentation is highly unreliable: it misses the entire wooden board stack, column, chair, and floor tools, hallucinates a 'skateboard' label on a wooden scrap near the co-worker's foot in frame 2 (~1.5 m away), fragments the co-worker's upper body around occluding boards in frames 4–5, and merges the co-worker's held board with their arm in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the five frames, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton for the co-worker's outstretched right hand in frame 1 (~1.3 m away, upper-right of centre) and a partial yellow body skeleton along a single arm-to-shoulder segment in frame 5 (~0.7 m away on the right). Using the RGB strip for context, frame 1's magenta keypoints mark the co-worker's left-reaching hand hovering within arm's reach (~0.3 m) of the upright wooden boards to the right of the central column, while the co-worker stands ~1.2–1.5 m from the camera wearer facing left and looking at the wood stack rather than at the camera wearer. In frame 5, the yellow segments trace the co-worker's extended left forearm and hand grasping an upright board ~0.5 m in front of their chest and ~0.3 m to the right of the camera wearer's own reaching left hand, though the keypoints also erroneously follow the straight edge of the wooden board itself. Aside from pinpointing the finger articulation of the reaching hand in frame 1, the pose map fails to capture the spatial layout, omitting the co-worker's full body and head across all frames, failing to detect any pose in frames 2–4 as the camera wearer approaches from ~1.5 m to ~0.6 m, and missing the camera wearer's own visible legs and reaching left arm in frames 3–5.
